dct_description_sm: Abstract: This datalayer is a polygon coverage which will display Massachusetts towns with associated data on population projections. The statistical data contained here were derived from MISER's (Massachusetts Institute for Social and Economic Research) Analysis of Components of Change in Population Projections for Massachusetts. These projections are revised biennially, taking into account information about trends in migration, births, and deaths. For more information on the definitions and enumeration process please read the "Supplemental Information" and "Attribute Accuracy Statement" (under Data Quality) sections which follow. This layer was derived from the Massachusetts Electronic Atlas database published by the Harvard Map Collection in 2001. The Massachusetts Electronic Atlas (MEA) was a collaborative project to provides access, via the Internet, to data about the Commonwealth, its thirteen regional planning agency districts and 351 cities and towns. This dataset is now only available via The Harvard Geospatial Library.

Purpose: This layer is intended for researchers, students, and policy makers for reference and mapping purposes, and may be used for basic applications such as viewing, querying, and map output production. This layer will provide a basemap for layers related to socio-political anaylsis, statistical enumeration and analysis, or to support graphical overlays and analysis with other spatial data. More advanced user applications may focus on demographics, urban and rural land use planning, socio-economic analysis and related areas including defining boundaries, managing assets and facilities, integrating attribute databases with geographic features, spatial analysis, and presentation output.

Supplemental information: The following information has been transcribed from the MISER website, availbale at: http://www.umass.edu/miser/population/index.html Why MISER produces different estimates than the U.S. Census Bureau: MISER has produced its own annual population estimates for the period 1991-1998 for all cities/towns in Massachusetts, attempting to improve the perceived underestimation of the population of the Commonwealth by the Census Bureau. In addition, MISER seeks to provide the public with more demographic information regarding population size and age, race-ethnicity, and sex structure at the sub-county level. This is not currently available from the Census Bureau's data products. To achieve this objective, MISER utilized additional and more detailed data sources and has also developed a new demographic model to estimate the Massachusetts population.
